conviction_note: The consensus row is NOT a mis-key: $0.44 is the mechanical output of Culp's own 2026-07-01 guide (breakeven-to-positive adjusted EBITDA ex-refund) plus the $7.0m IEEPA refund over 12.66m shares, with FY26 D&A of only $4.4m/yr and a full US valuation allowance - so the headline is unusually pre-determined and I expect a materially smaller absolute move than the baseline's 6.02% historical median, with a small positive tilt from three low-visibility mechanical points (53rd-week comp, guidance given with 9 of 13 weeks elapsed, no adjusted-EPS line to create a fake miss) net of a soft read-through from La-Z-Boy's overlapping quarter.

findings.finding: Q1 FY26 was a 14-week quarter ($50.7m of sales) because fiscal 2026 was a 53-week year, and Q1 FY27 is 13 weeks - so the $53.2m consensus is +4.9% on the headline but roughly +13% on a per-week like-for-like basis, and management's 'moderately improve versus the prior-year period' guide is a commitment to grow through the loss of a whole selling week.
findings.why_not_priced: No wire service, screener or estimate aggregator week-adjusts a 53-week fiscal year; the Q1 FY26 release buried it in the clause 'which included an extra week' and the $50.7m base is carried forward raw everywhere. If this were priced, the sell-side revenue estimate would sit near $49-50m (13/14ths of a flat comp) rather than $53.2m, and the pre-print commentary would frame the quarter as a like-for-like acceleration instead of a 5% YoY step-up. It sets up a release in which the YoY revenue and gross-margin comparisons understate the underlying improvement, which management will point out on the 10 Sept call.
findings.independence: The fiscal calendar is corroborated independently by the 10-K, whose fiscal year ends 2026-05-03 against the prior 2025-04-27 - 371 days, i.e. 53 weeks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm (filed 2026-07-17)

findings.finding: Culp issued its Q1 FY27 guidance on 2026-07-01 for a quarter that ended 2026-08-02 - i.e. with roughly 9 of 13 weeks already elapsed and the $7.0m tariff refund cash already in hand - so 'breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA without the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds' and 'net debt of approximately $5.0 million by first quarter-end' are near-observed facts, not forecasts.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline's expected move is a 6.02% median drawn from seven prints of which six went down - all of them delivered mid-restructuring with no forward guidance and genuinely uncertain outcomes. This print is the opposite: the guide was set two-thirds of the way through the quarter with the one-time cash already received. If the market had processed that the outcome distribution is narrow, the run-up would not be a directionless -0.58% over 20 days and the 5-day drift would not be a 17,000-share-a-day random walk; a stock about to resolve a genuinely uncertain 6% event trades differently into it. The residual is that Culp's downside tail here is much thinner than its own reaction history implies.
findings.independence: Shares a source document with finding 3 below (the 2026-07-01 EX-99.1) - flagging the cluster. Separately corroborated by the FY26 10-K, which reports only $4.426m of full-year D&A, meaning the EBITDA-to-EPS bridge is small and the guide translates almost directly into the reported number: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm

findings.finding: Culp presents adjusted EBITDA and 'non-GAAP operating loss' but no adjusted-EPS line at all, so the $7.0m IEEPA refund - 16% of the $43m market cap - flows into the single headline GAAP diluted EPS figure that wires will compare directly against the $0.44 estimate, with no adjusted/GAAP mismatch to manufacture a fake miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The default failure mode when a microcap books a one-time gain of this size is that the company headlines an ex-item loss and the tape prints a catastrophic-looking miss against a GAAP-basis estimate. That risk is real enough that if the market had checked it the estimate dispersion would show it - instead there is a single point estimate at $0.44 and no visible hedging. I checked the reconciliation captions in the company's own last release and the mismatch does not exist. This is a removed negative tail rather than new upside, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 2 - not independent, and the scorer should collapse these two to the larger. Nothing from a different source points the same way.

findings.finding: La-Z-Boy's fiscal Q1 ended 2026-07-25 - a window that overlaps Culp's 2026-05-04 to 2026-08-02 quarter almost exactly - showed consolidated sales down 3% to $476m with adjusted operating margin at 3.9% versus 4.8%, driven by expense deleverage on lower Wholesale and Joybird delivered sales; that is the single closest read-through to Culp's upholstery-fabrics segment, which produced $4.1m of Culp's $6.8m of Q4 gross profit.
findings.why_not_priced: This landed on 2026-08-18, seven weeks after Culp guided and after Culp's single covering analyst set the $53.2m/$0.44 model, so it is genuinely new information relative to what is in the estimate. Culp has no options, one estimate and 17,425 shares of average daily volume - there is no mechanism by which a supplier two tiers down gets remarked on a customer's print. If it were priced, the estimate would have been cut in late August and the 20-day run-up would be negative rather than flat. It is sized small and cuts against my other findings because La-Z-Boy's written orders were the opposite signal (+16% retail written, +3% written same-store), and fabric shipments lead furniture deliveries.
findings.independence: Same direction from ISPA's 2026 industry report, which shows US mattress unit shipments down 13.2% and market value down 6.5% year over year, bearing on Culp's bedding segment rather than upholstery: https://sleepproducts.org/2026/07/mattress-industry-trends-report-2026-overview/ (July 2026)

searched_and_found_nothing: The consensus row itself - $0.44 versus -$0.02 is NOT a mis-key or a different basis. It reconciles: guided breakeven-to-positive adjusted EBITDA ex-refund, plus the $7.0m refund, less ~$1.1m quarterly D&A (FY26 total was $4.426m), less ~$0.4m interest on $19.1m of debt, taxed lightly because of the full US valuation allowance, over 12,662,784 shares = roughly $0.40-$0.48. Estimate: https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/07/culp-culp-expected-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday.html

Whether the $7.0m refund is new information - it is not. It was disclosed in the 2026-07-01 Q4 FY26 release with the exact dollar figure, the receipt already in Q1 FY27, and a specific net-debt-of-$5.0m quarter-end target. The stock rose 11% on that print. Fully in the wire.

A post-IEEPA tariff-relief tailwind - killed. Section 122's 10% global surcharge expired 2026-07-24 and was replaced the same day by a Section 301 forced-labour action at 10%/12.5% covering 60 economies and 99.4% of US imports, so there is no step-down in Culp's input-tariff burden going into FY27. https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/07/us-administration-rebuilds-global-tariff-program-under-section-301 (2026-07-27)

Whether Haiti and the Dominican Republic - Culp's sewn-mattress-cover platform, historically duty-free under CBTPA/HOPE-HELP - are swept into the new 12.5% Section 301 tier. Could not confirm either way from the published country lists, which name only 17 economies at 10% and carve out USMCA. If they are covered it is a new cost from 2026-07-24, but I will not size an unconfirmed fact.

The five-filing Form 4 cluster of 2026-07-20 - routine post-fiscal-year-end grant timing, no open-market buying, and no Form 4 of any kind since. No insider signal.

Any 8-K between 2026-07-01 and today other than the 10-K, proxy and Section 16 filings - none. No credit-facility amendment, no covenant event, no equity issuance, no management change.

baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline: the history is 6 down out of 7 with a 6.02% median and there is no option chain or skew to argue with, but this print's headline is arithmetically closed by a guide the company issued with 9 of its 13 weeks already elapsed and the one-time cash already banked, so I expect both a smaller absolute move than the median and a small positive rather than the historical negative tilt.
